thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert from infra: high 5xx rate on inference-proxy us-west-2a (alert_id=pdp-8842)

ashwin (oncall): seeing 502/504s -> latency spiking on g5 nodes in us-west-2a. dashboard: https://console/redwood/metrics?panel=inference-proxy-usw2a . Any recent deploys? :eyes:

jess: no deploys from platform in the last hour. Autoscaler shows a bunch of 'unhealthy' targets on NLB for the us-west-2a pool.

mike: confirmed from packet captures — retransmits to instance i-0a1b2c3d4; connection resets and occasional ENETUNREACH on host.

laura-sre: copying logs: ```
[2026-03-15T18:12:02Z] proxy: conn reset to 10.12.8.47:443 state=closing
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] infra: kernel rx_queue overflow on eni eni-0f12a3
```

ev an-rt: (typo) evan-rt: probably RX drop pattern we've seen before with secondary egress. Could be noisy host-level interrupts. Quick check: is this limited to a subset of instances or whole AZ?

ashwin (oncall): it looks constrained to the g5.* pool in us-west-2a. Cross-AZ capacity in us-west-2b/c is healthy. Customer impact: 12% increase in host-level 5xx for hosted inference customers pinned to us-west-2a, some timeouts hitting retriable code path. CS flagged 3 customers with P95 token latency +200ms.

jess: starting mitigation plan: 1) drain NLB targets in the affected ENI set 2) reduce DNS TTL for region-level CNAME to 30s to speed steering 3) scale up replacement instances in other AZs and update routing policy with temporary weight shift. I'll run the drain now.

mike: before draining, we'd prefer graceful KV cache warmup fallback — draining instantly will force cold cache and increase latency. Suggest draining small batches (10%) and let Optimize apply prefix cache warmups.

ashwin (oncall): agree. Jess, drain in 10% increments every 90s. Mike, coordinate with Optimize to pre-warm caches for the target instances.

incident-bot: user impact summary: 24-minute window so far, errors mainly 502/504, approx 7% of requests retried by SDKs, estimated customer-facing errors ~0.8%. Automated reroutes triggered for high-priority customers.

laura-sre: I'm pausing new placements to us-west-2a at the infra layer (placement policy override) to prevent further scheduling there. Also opening a support ticket with AWS for host-level RX drops (submitted: 1234567890).

ev an-rt: I pushed a temporary routing override: set region-weight us-west-2a=50%, us-west-2b=25%, us-west-2c=25% (previously 70/15/15). This is under the routing service feature-flag so we can revert. Monitor for steady-state latency.

cs-rep: heads-up: CS will email affected customers with a short note — can we get a one-paragraph impact statement in the next 10m?

ashwin (oncall): short statement: "We observed elevated request errors and latency in one AWS availability zone (us-west-2a) which affected a subset of inference requests. We've routed traffic away from the affected hosts, are scaling capacity in other AZs, and engaged cloud vendor support. We'll post a follow-up with post-incident details." Feel free to edit.
mike: AWS support said hosts show NIC interrupt storm; they're escalating to their network team. Meanwhile, I've kicked off instance replacement for the 6 impacted nodes: `for id in i-0a1b2c3d4 i-0b2c3d4e5; do aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids $id; done`

jess: NLB drain started: batch1 10% (targets 6 -> draining), batch2 scheduled in 90s. Rolling monitor: dashboard shows requests shifting to us-west-2b/c, errors drop to baseline after batch2.

incident-bot: update: deployment telemetry — models on affected nodes show KV cache TTL expirations increased by 3x, small increase in token cost due to regen; Optimize alerted on cold-cache.

ashwin (oncall): switching high-priority customers to fallback model variant (quantized L2) for 30m to reduce tail latency while caches warm. Notifying feature flag system now.

laura-sre: AWS reply: investigating host NIC firmware — recommended to migrate instances off hosts; they've offered live migrate window ~15-20m but we already started instance replacement. They've also flagged potential local route flap on the AZ egress.

ev an-rt: metrics check: endpoint success rate for global traffic improved from 92% -> 99% after routing weight change + drains. P95 latency for HF model down from 1.9s -> 950ms. Good.

cs-rep: sending interim customer note now. Please add postmortem blurb when we have root cause.

mike: terminated nodes are being replaced in other AZs (placement policy) — also increased cross-AZ capacity by +15% to absorb any further AZ variability.

jess: switching DNS CNAME TTL back to 300s after we see stable traffic for 20m. Anyone opposed?

ashwin (oncall): fine to restore TTL once stable. Keep routing override in place until AWS confirms host fixes or until replaced nodes confirm healthy for 30m.

incident-bot: timeline event: 18:12 root alert. 18:16 routing override. 18:20 NLB drain batch1. 18:22 instance terminations. 18:32 errors approaching baseline. 18:40 DNS TTL restore planned at 19:05 once stable.

laura-sre: I'll take the incident lead for the postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: infra-runbooks to add ENI rx_queue monitoring alerts (owner: laura-sre), routing playbook to include cache warmup step before large drains (owner: mike), CS comms template (owner: cs-rep).

ashwin (oncall): on-call handoff note: I'm handing over to laura-sre at 19:00. No open critical actions other than monitoring for 30m and AWS ticket status.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by laura-sre.

laura-sre: taking over. I'll watch the dashboards and coordinate with AWS. If error rate spikes again, we revert routing weights and requeue any remaining drains.

cs-rep: customers notified. No escalations so far.

mike: final note — one short-term mitigation we tried that helped: limiting instance-level egress concurrent connections to 5000 for the affected nodes to reduce kernel queue pressure. Consider adding this knob to the autoscaler config.

jess: thanks team. I'll open the postmortem draft and include timeline + mitigations. Closing this slack thread when postmortem link posted. :slightly_smiling_face:
